Angular Introduction.exp: Introduction to Angular and its ecosystem.

Components: Components are the fundamental building blocks of Angular apps, each consisting of a TypeScript class, HTML template, and optional CSS styles. They control a view via a decorated class with @Component metadata.
Modules: NgModules organize an Angular app into cohesive blocks of functionality by declaring components, importing dependencies, and providing services. Every app has a root module (AppModule) as the entry point.
เทมเพลต (Template): Angular templates extend HTML with custom syntax including interpolation ({{ }}), property binding ([ ]), event binding (( )), and structural directives (*ngIf, *ngFor) for dynamic views.

Router: Angular Router enables navigation between views in SPAs with URL-based routing, nested routes, lazy-loaded modules, and route parameters. It integrates with the browser's history API.
Lazy Loading: Lazy loading loads feature modules on demand when the user navigates to their routes, reducing initial bundle size. Use loadChildren in route config to point to a module imported via dynamic import.
Guards: Route guards control navigation using interfaces like CanActivate, CanDeactivate, and Resolve. They prevent unauthorized access, prompt for unsaved changes, and pre-fetch data before a route activates.

Angular Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Angular.

Jasmine: Jasmine is a behavior-driven development framework for testing JavaScript code with a clean, readable syntax. It provides describe/it blocks, matchers (toEqual, toContain), and spies.
Karma: Karma is a test runner that executes tests in real browsers, providing fast feedback loops and reporting. It's the default test runner in Angular CLI projects via ng test.
TestBed: TestBed is Angular's primary testing utility for configuring and creating component test environments. It manages module compilation, dependency injection, and provides ComponentFixture for interaction.

Dependency Injection: Angular's dependency injection system provides dependencies to classes via constructor parameters. The injector hierarchy creates singleton or per-component instances of services automatically.
Services: Services are singleton classes decorated with @Injectable that encapsulate business logic, data access, or cross-cutting concerns. They are the recommended way to share logic between components.
Providers: Providers configure the injector with dependency recipes, controlling how services are created and scoped. They can be registered at module level, component level, or using providedIn: 'root' for tree-shaking.

Template-driven: Template-driven forms rely on directives in the template like ngModel for two-way data binding. They are simpler but less scalable than reactive forms, suitable for basic form use cases.
Reactive: Reactive forms provide a model-driven approach with form control instances created programmatically, offering more predictability, testability, and advanced validation capabilities.
Validation: Angular forms support built-in validators (required, minLength, pattern) and custom async validators. Validation state is exposed through CSS classes (ng-valid, ng-invalid) and component properties.

HttpClient: HttpClient is Angular's built-in HTTP client with typed request/response, interceptors, and automatic JSON parsing. Methods return Observables supporting RxJS operators for transformations.
Interceptors: Interceptors sit between the application and the backend, transforming outgoing requests or incoming responses. Common use cases include adding auth tokens, logging, and error handling.
การจัดการข้อผิดพลาด: Error handling in HTTP requests is done via RxJS catchError operator, retrying failed requests, or displaying user-friendly error messages. Global error handling can be centralized in interceptors.

Directives: Angular offers three types of directives: components, structural directives (alter DOM layout), and attribute directives (change appearance or behavior). Custom directives encapsulate reusable DOM manipulation.
Pipes: Pipes transform data in templates for display, such as formatting dates, currencies, or filtering lists. Angular provides built-in pipes and you can create custom pure or impure pipes.
Custom Decorators: Decorators are TypeScript features used extensively in Angular for metadata. Custom decorators can extend component behavior, add logging, or transform class properties at design time.

Change Detection: Angular's default change detection checks every component in the tree when any data changes, ensuring consistency. It uses zone.js to patch browser APIs and trigger checks automatically.
OnPush: OnPush change detection strategy reduces unnecessary checks by only running detection when input references change, events fire, or observables emit. It's essential for large lists and performance-critical views.
Code Splitting: Angular supports code splitting through lazy-loaded modules and ES dynamic imports. The CLI generates separate chunks per lazy route, and the router loads them on demand when the user navigates.

Standalone API: Standalone components, directives, and pipes are self-contained without needing NgModules. Created with the standalone: true flag, they import dependencies directly and can be lazy-loaded via the router.
Bootstrap Standalone: Applications can bootstrap directly from a standalone component instead of NgModule. The main.ts calls bootstrapApplication with the root component and optional provider configuration.
Routing Standalone: Standalone components load lazily with loadComponent in the route config, eliminating the need for feature modules. Each route points directly to a component with its own imports.

Writable Signals: Signals are reactive primitives that notify consumers when their value changes. Writable signals created with signal() expose get/set/update methods for synchronous state management.
Computed Signals: Computed signals derive values from other signals with lazy evaluation and caching. They only recompute when dependent signals change, replacing manual ChangeDetectorRef calls.
Effects: Effects run side effects automatically when their signal dependencies change. They are used for syncing state to localStorage, logging, or triggering imperative DOM operations.
Signal Inputs: Signal-based inputs replace @Input with input() and input.required(), providing reactive input values without lifecycle hooks. They integrate natively with the change detection system.

ng generate: The Angular CLI generates components, directives, pipes, services, modules, and more using ng generate. Schematics customize generation with options for style, inline template, and routing.

ng generate component dashboard --standalone --inline-style --skip-tests
ng generate service api/data
ng generate module admin --route admin --module app
Custom Schematics: Custom schematics automate project scaffolding by generating files, modifying existing code, and installing dependencies. They are published as npm packages and run with ng generate.
Angular Builders: Builders extend the Angular CLI build pipeline with custom build, test, or deploy logic. They replace Angular's default builder to support custom tooling like custom webpack configs.

@defer: Deferrable views (introduced in Angular 17) lazy-load component dependencies with @defer blocks. They improve initial bundle size by deferring heavy components until a specified trigger.
Defer Triggers: Defer triggers control when lazy content loads: on viewport (enters viewport), on interaction (user clicks), on immediate, on idle (browser idle), or on a custom timer.
Defer Dependencies: Deferred components and their transitive dependencies are split into separate JavaScript chunks. Angular loads these chunks asynchronously when the trigger condition is met, reducing initial payload.

inject(): The inject() function provides a programmatic alternative to constructor-based dependency injection. It can be called in the class body, making DI more flexible and reducing boilerplate.
Injection Context: inject() must be called within an injection context such as a constructor, class field initializer, or factory function. Outside these contexts it throws, ensuring predictable DI resolution.

Angular Signals Deep Dive: Angular Signals provide reactive state management with fine-grained reactivity. Unlike Zone.js-based change detection (which checks the entire component tree), Signals track dependencies automatically and update only affected consumers. Key APIs: signal() creates a writable signal, computed() creates derived values, effect() runs side effects when signal values change. The new control flow (@if, @for, @switch) replaces *ngIf, *ngFor, and ngSwitch with better type narrowing and performance. Standalone components are now the default — NgModules are optional.
Angular Routing & Lazy Loading: Angular Router enables SPA navigation with lazy-loaded feature modules/routes. Routes are defined as an array of Route objects with path, component or loadComponent (standalone) / loadChildren (modules). canActivate, canDeactivate, and canLoad guards protect routes. Resolve fetches data before route activation. Route params (paramMap, queryParamMap) are accessible via ActivatedRoute. PreloadingStrategy (PreloadAllModules, custom strategies) balances initial bundle size with subsequent navigation speed. Router events (NavigationStart, NavigationEnd, NavigationError) enable loading indicators.
Angular Forms & Validation: Angular provides two form approaches: Template-driven Forms (simpler, suitable for basic forms) and Reactive Forms (more flexible, suitable for complex forms, better testing). Reactive Forms use FormControl, FormGroup, and FormArray with explicit validation via Validators. Custom validators extend validation logic. Async validators call servers (e.g., checking username availability). Form arrays handle dynamic form fields. ValueChanges observable enables reactive form interactions. Typed forms (Angular 14+) provide strict typing for form values.

Testing Components & Services: Angular Testing uses TestBed for configuring modules, creating components, and injecting services. ComponentFixture provides component instance and debug element. async() and fakeAsync() handle asynchronous operations. HttpClientTestingModule and HttpTestingController mock HTTP requests. Use By.css() for DOM querying and DetectChanges() to trigger change detection. Component harnesses (CDK) provide a stable API for interacting with components in tests. Override providers in TestBed to mock services. E2E tests use Playwright or Cypress.
Angular Performance Optimization: Angular performance optimization: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush reduces change detection to only when inputs change or events fire. trackBy in @for/ngFor prevents unnecessary DOM re-creation. Lazy loading reduces initial bundle size. @defer (Angular 17+) defers loading of heavy components until viewport or interaction. provideZoneFlush with NoopZone enables zoneless change detection with signals. pure pipes prevent recalculation. Server-Side Rendering (SSR) with Angular Universal improves initial load. Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) guide performance targets.
